accepted.question_text: Let X be a nonsingular projective variety over C, let M_g(X, β) be the moduli space of stable maps to X in curve class β, and let π: M_g(X, β) → M_g be the morphism that forgets the map and remembers only the domain curve. The moduli space M_g(X, β) carries a virtual fundamental class [M_g(X, β)]^vir. Does the pushed-forward class π_*[M_g(X, β)]^vir in the cohomology H_*(M_g) always lie in the tautological ring of M_g?
accepted.context_brief: Virtual classes and tautological cohomology on moduli of curves

evidence.quote: Let X be a nonsingular, projective variety over C. Let Mg(X, β) be the moduli space of stable maps and let π : Mg(X, β) → Mg be the forgetful morphism
Q1. Does π∗[Mg(X, β)]vir ∈ H∗(Mg) lie in the tautological ring in cohomology?

accepted.question_text: Under what conditions on a nonsingular projective variety X over C and curve class β does the pushed-forward virtual fundamental class π_*[M_g(X, β)]^vir of the moduli space of stable maps lie in the tautological ring of the Chow ring A_*(M_g), where π: M_g(X, β) → M_g is the forgetful morphism to the moduli space of curves?
accepted.context_brief: Virtual classes and tautological Chow classes

evidence.quote: The moduli space of stable maps carries a virtual class [Mg(X, β)]vir obtained from deformation theory
Q2. When does π∗[Mg(X, β)]vir ∈ A∗(Mg) lie in the tautological ring in Chow?

accepted.question_text: Prove the Virasoro constraints for the Gromov–Witten theory of an Enriques surface. Here the Gromov–Witten invariants are the invariants determined by the moduli spaces M_g(X, β) of stable maps to X, and the paper identifies the Enriques surface as a basic case in which the Virasoro constraints are still unknown.

evidence.quote: These are conjectured to satisfy the Virasoro constraints [4]. Virasoro constraints are known to hold now in many, but not all, cases [8, 14]. A very interesting variety for which the Virasoro constraints are unknown is the Enriques surface.
Q3. Prove the Virasoro constraints in case X is an Enriques surface.

accepted.question_text: Let X be a nonsingular projective 3-fold. Prove the Gromov–Witten/Donaldson–Thomas correspondence for X: the paper states that the Gromov–Witten theory of X, defined via the moduli spaces M_g(X, β) of stable maps, is conjecturally equivalent to the Donaldson–Thomas theory of X, which is defined using moduli of ideal sheaves of curves in X or, more recently, moduli spaces of stable pairs.

evidence.quote: Let X be a nonsingular, projective 3-fold. The Gromov-Witten theory of X, defined via Mg(X, β), is conjecturally [15] equivalent to the Donaldson-Thomas theory of X. The latter is defined via the moduli of ideal sheaves of curves in X [3, 25], or more recently, in terms of the moduli spaces of stable pairs [22].
Q4. Prove the GW/DT correspondence for 3-folds.

accepted.question_text: Define Donaldson–Thomas invariants for varieties of dimension greater than 3. The motivating issue stated in the paper is that the usual definition in dimension 3 depends on having a virtual fundamental class for a moduli space of sheaves, with deformations controlled by Ext^1(E,E), obstructions by Ext^2(E,E), and a needed vanishing of Ext^i(E,E) for i > 2; the problem asks for an analogue beyond the 3-dimensional setting.

evidence.quote: Donaldson–Thomas invariants are defined only in dimension 3 because a virtual fundamental class for the moduli space of sheaves is required. Deformations are given by Ext1(E, E), obstructions by Ext2(E, E), and to define the virtual fundamental class we need (roughly) the vanishing Exti(E, E) = 0 for i > 2 .
Q5. Define Donaldson–Thomas invariants in dimensions > 3.

accepted.question_text: Let M_{2n}^{K3} denote the moduli space of polarized K3 surfaces (S, L) of degree L^2 = 2n. What should play the role of the tautological ring for M_{2n}^{K3}? The paper frames this as a question in the cycle theory of the moduli space and suggests the subring generated by classes of Noether–Lefschetz loci as a natural candidate.
accepted.context_brief: Tautological-type ring for polarized K3 moduli

evidence.quote: Let MK3 2n denote the moduli space of polarized K3 surfaces (S, L) of degree L2 = 2n. Little appears to be known about the cycle theory of MK3 2n.
Q6. What is the analogue of the tautological ring for MK3 2n ?
A natural guess for Q6 is the subring generated by the classes of the Noether–Lefschetz loci.

accepted.question_text: Let M_{2n}^{K3} be the moduli space of polarized K3 surfaces of degree 2n. Do the Noether–Lefschetz divisors span the rational Picard group Pic(M_{2n}^{K3}) ⊗_Z Q?
accepted.context_brief: Picard group of polarized K3 moduli

evidence.quote: The Noether-Lefschetz loci parameterize K3 surfaces with higher rank Picard lattices.
Q7. Do the Noether-Lefschetz divisors span Pic(MK3 2n ) ⊗Z Q?

accepted.question_text: Prove the Katz–Klemm–Vafa conjecture for K3 surfaces in every genus and for every curve class. In the paper, this conjecture concerns λ_g integrals in the reduced Gromov–Witten theory of a fixed K3 surface and appears in the study of K3-fibered Calabi–Yau 3-folds via Noether–Lefschetz theory.

evidence.quote: Via [19], the Gromov-Witten theory of X in π-fiber classes is calculated in terms of the Noether–Lefschetz numbers of π and the Katz-Klemm-Vafa [10] conjecture concerning λg integrals in the reduced Gromov-Witten theory of a fixed K3 surface.
Q8. Prove the Katz-Klemm-Vafa conjecture for in all genera and in all classes on K3 surfaces.

accepted.question_text: Find effective mathematical methods for computing the higher-genus Gromov–Witten invariants of compact Calabi–Yau 3-folds. The paper presents this as a general problem motivated by the fact that exact formulas would follow from progress on the KKV conjecture for K3 surfaces, while existing mathematical methods are still less effective than the holomorphic anomaly equation from topological string theory in many examples.
accepted.context_brief: Effective higher-genus GW methods for compact Calabi–Yau 3-folds

evidence.quote: A solution to Q8 would provide a large class of exact formulas for higher genus Gromov-Witten invariants of compact Calabi-Yau 3-folds.
Q9. Find effective mathematical methods for calculating the higher genus Gromov-Witten invariants of compact Calabi-Yau 3-folds.
